**Answer** I don’t have direct access to the Internet right now, so I can’t pull a fresh “now‑on‑screen” list from your local cinema chain or streaming service. Below you’ll find: 1. A quick guide on where to look for the most up‑to‑date release lists. 2. An example script that uses **TMDb’s public API** (or another similar database) to programmatically retrieve the newest releases at runtime. --- ### 1️⃣ Where to check the latest releases | Platform / Service | How to view | |--------------------|-------------| | **Local theater chains** (AMC, Regal, Cinemark, etc.) | Visit their website → *Now Showing* section. Many also offer mobile apps. | | **Streaming services** (Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, Apple TV+) | Each has a dedicated “New Releases” or “Recently Added” page. | | **Movie‑tracking websites** | • [IMDb](https://www.imdb.com/movies-coming-soon/) – shows upcoming & newly released films.
• [TasteDive](https://tastedive.com/), [Letterboxd](https://letterboxd.com/films/upcoming/). | | **Cinema aggregator apps** | Apps such as Fandango, Flixster, or Google Play Movies often display both theatrical and digital premieres. | If you’re looking for something specific—like indie releases, foreign-language films, or blockbusters—you can usually filter within those interfaces. --- ### 2️⃣ Programmatic retrieval (Python) Many developers prefer pulling this data automatically—for instance, building a bot that posts daily film news. One popular free source is **The Movie Database (TMDb)**. Below is a minimal working example that prints out the top‑rated movies added in the past week. ```python import requests from datetime import datetime, timedelta API_KEY = "" # Sign up here: https://developers.themoviedb.org/ BASE_URL = "https://api.themoviedb.org/3" def get_recent_releases(days=7): """ Fetches movies released in the last `days` days. Parameters: days (int): Number of days back from today to consider. Returns: List[dict]: Each dict contains title, release_date, overview, rating, etc. """ end_date = datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%d") start_date = (datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=days)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d") params = { "api_key": API_KEY, "language": "en-US", "sort_by": "primary_release_date.asc", # ascending order "include_adult": False, "page": 1, "region": "US", "release_date.lte": end_date, "release_date.gte": start_date, } url = f"{BASE_URL}/discover/movie" resp = requests.get(url, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() results = resp.json()["results"] return [ { "title": r["original_title"], "release_date": r["release_date"], "overview": r["overview"][:200], # truncate long descriptions "rating": r["vote_average"], "popularity": r["popularity"] } for r in results ] if __name__ == "__main__": recent_movies = get_recent_releases(10) # change to whatever window you care about print(f"Movies released in the last {len(recent_movies)} days:") for idx, mv in enumerate(sorted(recent_movies, key=lambda x: x['release_date'])): print(f"\n{idx+1}. {mv['title']} ({mv['release_date']})") print(f"Rating: {mv['rating']} ★ | Popularity: {mv['popularity']}") print(f"Overview: {mv['overview']}\n{'-'*60}") ``` #### What you need to run it 1. Create a free account on TMDb and obtain an API key (`` above). 2. Install dependencies: `pip install requests`. 3. Run the script. It will output all movies whose US release dates fall within the specified range. Feel free to tweak parameters: - Change `"region"` to match your country (e.g., `"JP"` for Japan). - Use `"with_genres"` to filter by genre ID (see TMDb docs). - Add pagination handling if you expect more than one page of results. --- ### Quick recap | Task | Suggested method | |------|------------------| | Browse manually | Theater chain site / Streaming app | | Get instant alerts | Set up a small cron job running the snippet above | | Build a custom dashboard | Combine multiple APIs (TMDb + Rotten Tomatoes + Box Office Mojo) into a single JSON feed | Let me know if you'd like help setting up a scheduled task, integrating other sources, or tailoring the search criteria!
